svg.title: Figure 2. Runtime loop and attack surface
svg.desc: Instruction, planning, tool selection, tool execution, tool result, and re-plan. Memory and peer are conditional. Gates are not on this path.
svg.text: This is the system under test. Gates G1–G4 are not steps in this loop. An attempt is not the scored effect. The effect is the pre-declared check on the trace.

text.tspan: Manual or schema text.
C3 stores the pin and hash in the manifest.
Code behind the tool name.
C4 pins the hash and permission, or records a
waiver.
Recorded levels, or one level.
Not a separate attack surface.
The user task enters here.
In scope only when the check is a tool,
memory, or peer effect.
Plan text may be stored.
It is marked non-oracle.
C5 compares it with a later call and does not
stop that call.
The chosen tool name.
C3: the name matches the pinned manual.
The description is not the implementation.
Arguments, destination, channel class, and the
committed flag.
C2 applies the allow-list before commit.
C4 applies when tool code is in scope.
Tool result, page, email, or retrieved passage.
C1 keeps that text in the data channel.
It is not copied into the instruction channel.

svg.text: MEMORY BRANCH · present only when Stage 1 registers memory. A waiver removes the whole branch, including C8.

text.tspan: Operation, entry identifier, and
provenance.
A write is not an outbound call.
Same entry fields on a later read.
A read is not an outbound call.
Drawn only when the call is observed after a relevant read.
C8 does not follow every C7 event.
If memory is waived, this node is absent.
Not applicable is a scope state, not a pass.

svg.text: OFF THE LOOP · commit and recovery are not steps of the solid loop

text.tspan: Detect, then respond: leave the committed flag false, or record approval
of that call.
A detector flag is not evidence that the effect was stopped.
A post-commit flag is a late detection, not a miss.
Quarantine or delete the entry, roll back a reversible effect, or list the
residual.
A restore that is not rerun is not recovery.
Recovery-rerun task success is Stage 9, not this arrow.
Dashed: only if Stage 1 registers a peer.
Log sender, receiver, message identifier, and the receiver’s next tool call.
Not a step after memory. The score stays in a separate table.
The carrier is where untrusted content can enter.
The check is the later observable effect.
Placing a carrier is an attempt, not attack success.

svg.text: Untrusted content — tool result, page, email, retrieval
Tool description — separate from tool implementation
Tool implementation — the effect, not the manual
Tool selection — the chosen tool name
Tool execution — name, arguments, destination, commit
Tool result — data channel, not a new instruction
Memory write, then a later read — C7
Outbound call after a relevant read — C8, only if observed
Peer message — only if a peer is registered
Instruction channel — only as a tool, memory, or peer effect

text.tspan: A waiver of tool code, memory, or peers removes that branch.
The waiver is a scope note. It is not a surface and not a pass.
A chat-only jailbreak has no check on this loop.
Prevent — C1, C2, C3, C4; also the prevent part of C7, C8, C9
Detect — C5; also the detect part of C6, C7, C9
Respond — C6 blocks or records approval; C9 can drop the message
Recover — C10, after commit, and only if the restore is rerun
Dashed outline — drawn only when Stage 1 registers that component

svg.text: C5 does not stop the call. A memory read does not create C8. Gates are on Figures 1 and 5. No control on this figure has been measured.
